description: Who promised what, by when, in both directions. Yours become tasks and are verified like any task. Theirs are the underused half: an unmet customer commitment — the security questionnaire that never arrived, the intro to the VP that never happened — is one of the earliest stall signals a deal gives off, and until this registry existed nothing was in a position to notice it.

columns.name: meeting_id
columns.note: The MTG- row this came out of. A commitment with no meeting behind it was never actually made.

columns.name: direction
columns.note: ours = we promised it (raise a task, verify it happened). theirs = they promised it (watch for it; chase it gently when overdue; read a pattern of broken ones as the stall signal it is).

columns.name: who
columns.note: The person who made the commitment, by name.

columns.name: what
columns.note: The commitment in the words it was made in, specific enough to verify: 'send the SOC 2 report', not 'follow up on security'.

columns.name: due_date
columns.note: When it was promised for. Blank when no date was given — which is itself worth noticing, and worth pinning down in the follow-up email. Overdue is computed on read: status Open and due_date past.

columns.name: status
columns.note: There is deliberately no 'Overdue' value — overdue is Open plus a past due_date, computed when read, so it can never go stale in the file.

columns.name: evidence
columns.note: How we know it was met — the email that arrived, the meeting that happened. For ours, the task's verification usually settles it.

columns.name: task_id
columns.note: For direction ours: the TASK- row that carries it. The task machinery owns drafting, automation posture and verification; this row owns the fact that it was promised.
